title: Waveform-aware KV fragment scheduler and decode fairness controller
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: We observe recurring tail-latency spikes when workloads exhibit high temporal locality followed by deep long-tail queries ("waveforms"). These spikes correlate with heavy KV fragment churn: small fragmented pages cause kernel choices to fall back to conservative decode paths and cause frequent prefill misses. Goal: build a scheduler that recognizes waveform patterns in request streams and adapts allocation, eviction, kernel hints, and prefill pacing to reduce tail P99 decode latency while preserving overall throughput and cache reuse. The feature will: 1) maintain short-term quantile models of request span distribution (waveform profiles) per route/tenant; 2) drive a slot reservation allocator that pre-allocates contiguous slots for predicted near-future spans to reduce fragmentation; 3) attach kernel selection hints to prefill ops so the serving runtime can choose compact kernels for fragmented hot pages and wider kernels for stable residency pages; 4) add a decode-fairness controller that enforces soft quotas to prevent single long spans from starving small latency-sensitive calls. This work targets both hosted and Dedicated modes and must be instrumentation-rich for gradual rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce P99 decode latency for waveform-heavy benchmarks by >=25% compared to baseline on ci-serving-lab-2
Prefill miss rate (KB-level) decreased by >=18% for the synthetic waveform load with identical token throughput
No regression (>5%) in aggregate token throughput on replications of current 95th percentile CPU/GPU utilization tests
Integration tests for allocator invariants and kernel-hint path coverage in unit/e2e harness
Feature gated behind runtime flag and rolloutable per-tenant via Console; rollout plan documented
implementation_notes: Introduce WaveformProfiler: sliding-quantile sketch keyed by (route, tenant, model) to estimate upcoming span length distribution
SlotAllocator: reservation window that can coalesce adjacent small fragments into a temporary contiguous reservation using soft locks
Eviction policy: demote candidates that would raise fragmentation score; add compaction hint to background GC
Kernel hints: annotate prefill request metadata with 'frag_score' and 'reservation_stability' to allow kernel selector to prefer smaller working sets or alternative kernels
DecodeFairnessController: token-budget scheduler using token-slices per active request and starvation detection with corrective backoffs
Metrics: add waveform_profile_{p50,p75,p90,p99}, frag_score, reservation_success_rate, decode_slice_starvation_count
Ensure changes compile on both x86 CUDA and ARM ROCm CI runners; include fallback paths for unknown hints

risks: Risk: Waveform profiling introduces additional CPU overhead and memory for sketches—mitigate with sampling and bounded sketch size
Risk: Reservation window can increase transient memory pressure under multi-tenant high concurrency—address with per-tenant soft guardrails
Risk: Kernel hints may interact unpredictably with existing kernel autoscaler; require careful A/B and fallback logic
Risk: Fairness controller could reduce throughput for long-batch offline workloads if misconfigured—expose tenant-level opt-outs
testing_plan: Unit tests for profiler quantiles and slot reservation correctness
Simulator tests that replay production trace slices (including incident traces) to measure fragmentation dynamics
CI e2e using ci-serving-lab-2 with synthetic waveform generator (multiple amplitude/frequency configs)
Canary on dedicated pool with telemetry: decode P50/P95/P99, reservation_success_rate, frag_score, and token-cost delta
Chaos: short prefill flood + eviction storms to ensure graceful degradation and background compaction
